title: CBC News Broadcast: Full Interview w/ Freeman On The Land - Rob Menard
summary: CBC interview with a Canadian freeman-on-the-land promoter on claims of right, the right to travel, income tax, birth-certificate accounts and police.

assertions.quote: if all you're doing is engaging in travel you're going from point A to point B and you are not engaging in Commerce
when you register anything from your car your property your children essentially what you're doing is you're signing it over

verdicts.note: Registration records ownership or a birth; it does not transfer title to the state.

assertions.quote: we do have the right to establish lawful excuse to disobey the government

verdicts.note: Canadian courts, notably in Meads v Meads, hold such notices have no legal effect.
The 'claim of right' motif already appears, rejected, in decisions Meads compiled; the NZ statutory defence relied on was later abolished and the protesters held liable.
The 'Notice of Understanding, Intent and Claim of Right' is the Freeman opt-out document; cases using it failed and its promoter pled guilty to a transit offence he claimed immunity from.
The Freeman 'Notice of Understanding, Intent, and Claim of Right' is meant to withdraw consent, but unilateral rejection of state authority was refused leave as having no legal merit.

assertions.quote: if the bank has not suffered a loss then you don't owe them anything

verdicts.note: A loan contract obliges repayment whether or not the lender sold the note; vapour-money arguments are uniformly rejected.

assertions.quote: when you work and you get paid a wage that's not even really income

verdicts.note: Courts uniformly treat wages as income; the argument is a listed frivolous position in the US and rejected by the CRA in Canada.

IRC 61 defines gross income to include compensation for services, and appellate courts (e.g. 3d Cir. Connor: every court has unequivocally rejected the argument that wages are not income) sanction the contrary argument.

assertions.quote: if you don't have a social insurance number you do not have an account with CRA

verdicts.note: Tax liability depends on income and residence, not on holding an identifying number.
One guru was acquitted because the Crown failed to link him to his SIN, but that reasoning was later rejected; it did not free anyone from income tax.
